_comment: FICTITIOUS sample data for demonstrating the S3 Data Protection Advisor report. AnyCompany Health and every account ID, bucket name, size and cost below are invented. Account IDs are AWS documentation example IDs.

third_party.evidence: Bucket names anycompany-veeam-repo-prod and anycompany-veaam-offsite (misspelling, lower confidence) + IAM role AnyCompanyVeeamBackupRole

buckets.name: anycompany-invoices-prod
buckets.write_pattern: Write-once / Append: +59M objects/day, 0 deletes over 30 days

findings.title: 20 PiB of invoices unversioned, but they are never overwritten
findings.description: Objects are written once and never changed or deleted (30-day CloudWatch metrics). Versioning protects every invoice against accidental or scripted deletion for about $950/month (about 0.2% of its storage bill), because no noncurrent versions are created.
findings.action: Enable versioning (Quick Win: ~$950/month) with a 30-day NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule

findings.title: SSE-KMS without S3 Bucket Keys
findings.description: 59M new objects/day each trigger a KMS request. Bucket Keys cut KMS request cost by up to 99%.

buckets.name: anycompany-imaging-archive-2019
buckets.write_pattern: Static: object count and size unchanged for 30 days

findings.title: 60 PiB medical-imaging archive can be deleted with one API call
findings.description: The archive is completely static, so versioning costs $0 (measured). It is the largest dataset in the estate and has no second copy.
findings.action: Enable versioning ($0, measured), then Object Lock (Governance) for the retention period

findings.title: Largest dataset exists in one region only
findings.description: No replication and no AWS Backup coverage. To confirm whether the imaging archive can be re-acquired from source systems.
findings.action: Confirm re-derivability; if not re-derivable, replicate to Deep Archive in eu-central-1 (estimate ~$110,600/month + ~$1.23M one-time transfer)

buckets.name: anycompany-session-state-prod
buckets.write_pattern: Overwrite-heavy: same keys rewritten, ~60% of bytes per month (request metrics)

findings.title: Overwrite-heavy bucket: versioning is cheap only with a short noncurrent expiration
findings.description: About 60% of the bytes are rewritten each month. With a 7-day NoncurrentVersionExpiration, versioning costs ~$1,300/month (measured); without the rule it grows by ~240 TiB every month. If session state is ephemeral by design, document that and leave it unversioned.
findings.action: Confirm the data is worth protecting; if so, enable versioning WITH a 7-day NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule (~$1,300/month)

findings.title: Signed legal contracts exist in a single region
findings.description: Versioning protects against accidental deletion, but there is no cross-region copy and no backup. Legal records can't be re-created, so a regional disruption or account compromise means permanent loss.
findings.action: Add cross-region replication to eu-central-1 Deep Archive (estimate ~$5,530/month + ~$61,400 one-time transfer)

findings.title: No Object Lock on records with a legal retention obligation
findings.description: Any principal with s3:DeleteObjectVersion can purge history. Object Lock in Compliance mode enforces the retention period, which is also what auditors ask for.
findings.action: Enable Object Lock (Compliance) with the legal retention period on new objects; apply retention to existing objects with S3 Batch Operations

findings.title: Versioning was suspended on the payments bucket
findings.description: Older versions are still retained, but every object written since suspension is unprotected against overwrite and deletion. Suspension is often a one-off cost fix that was never reverted.
findings.action: Re-enable versioning (currently Suspended) and add a NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule

findings.title: CloudTrail audit trail can be deleted
findings.description: An attacker who gains write access can erase the record of what they did. Tamper-evidence is the point of an audit trail.
findings.action: Enable versioning + Object Lock (Governance, 365 days) and a lifecycle rule to Glacier after 90 days

findings.title: US orders bucket has none of the protections of its EU twin
findings.description: The eu-west-1 deployment has versioning, Object Lock (Governance 30d), SSE-KMS and a daily AWS Backup plan. The us-east-1 copy of the same application has none of them, and AWS Backup for S3 isn't enabled in us-east-1.
findings.action: Align with anycompany-orders-prod-eu-west-1: enable versioning, Object Lock (Governance 30d), SSE-KMS; opt S3 in to AWS Backup in us-east-1

findings.title: Reference configuration: protected from all three risks
findings.description: Versioning, Object Lock Compliance 7 years, CRR to a locked replica in eu-central-1, and continuous AWS Backup. Use this bucket as the template for other regulated data.

buckets.name: anycompany-partner-exchange-prod-eu-west-1
buckets.write_pattern: Transient: files picked up and deleted within 24h
buckets.note: GetObjectLockConfiguration and GetBucketReplication returned AccessDenied (bucket policy restricts the analysis role).

buckets.name: anycompany-partner-exchange-prod-us-east-1
buckets.write_pattern: Transient: files picked up and deleted within 24h

findings.title: Bucket named 'public-test' with no public-access guardrail at any level
findings.description: Bucket-level Block Public Access is off, and so is account-level BPA in the Production account.
findings.action: Enable bucket-level Block Public Access; delete the bucket if the test is over

buckets.name: anycompany-datalake-raw
buckets.write_pattern: Overwrite-heavy: daily re-ingest rewrites ~8% of bytes per month

findings.title: Versioned without lifecycle: noncurrent versions grow forever
findings.description: ~600 TiB of noncurrent versions is added every month and never expires: estimate +$14,100/month, every month, unbounded. After a year that's ~7 PiB of hidden storage.

buckets.name: anycompany-research-datasets-prod
buckets.write_pattern: Append-mostly: new study data added monthly

findings.title: 30 PiB in S3 Standard with no tiering: up to ~$465,000/month to save with Intelligent-Tiering
findings.description: All 30 PiB is billed at the Standard rate (estimate $706,600/month) and no lifecycle rule moves data to a cheaper class. The access pattern is not visible in configuration metadata, so confirm it. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is low-risk either way: it moves objects to Infrequent Access after 30 days and Archive Instant Access after 90 days without access, has no retrieval fees and keeps millisecond access. Worst case (everything read often): +~$15,000/month monitoring fee for 6B objects. If, as is typical for research datasets, ~70% of the data goes unread for 90+ days: ~$242,000/month instead of $706,600, saving up to ~$465,000/month (~$5.6M/year). One-time transition: ~$60,000.
findings.action: Confirm the access pattern , then add a lifecycle rule transitioning current versions to S3 Intelligent-Tiering (estimate: up to ~$465,000/month saving, worst case +$15,000/month; ~$60,000 one-time)

findings.title: A replica is not a backup: deletions replicate too
findings.description: Delete-marker replication is on and the replica has no Object Lock, so a deletion (accidental or malicious) in eu-west-1 reaches eu-central-1 within minutes. The replica covers a regional outage, not deletion.
findings.action: Enable Object Lock (Governance) on the replica, or turn off delete-marker replication if downstream jobs don't need it

findings.title: scans-003 drifted from its series
findings.description: scans-001, -002 and -004 are versioned; -003 (the only one in us-east-1) never was. It is static, so versioning costs $0 (measured).
findings.action: Enable versioning ($0, measured) to match scans-001/002/004

buckets.name: anycompany-veeam-repo-prod
buckets.write_pattern: Append + daily retention cleanup by Veeam

findings.title: Veeam repository (42.5 PiB) is not immutable
findings.description: Versioning is on, but there is no Object Lock, so Veeam's immutability option can't be active. Anyone holding the Veeam service credentials (a typical ransomware target) can delete every restore point, versions included. This is the copy of last resort.
findings.action: Create an Object Lock-enabled bucket and enable Veeam immutability on the repository (move backups with a new chain); keep versioning

findings.title: Off-site Veeam copy (20 PiB) has no versioning and no Object Lock
findings.description: Detected as a Veeam target despite the misspelled name ('veaam'). The off-site copy exists to survive the loss of the primary, yet it is fully mutable.
findings.action: Enable versioning + Object Lock (Governance) or Veeam immutability (estimate ~$4,100/month)

buckets.name: anycompany-sqlserver-fullbkp
buckets.write_pattern: Rotation: nightly full dumps, deleted after 14 days

findings.title: Database dumps can be deleted along with the database
findings.description: Nightly SQL Server full backups land here (name signature 'fullbkp') with no versioning or lock. Because dumps rotate every 14 days, versioning is not free: ~$5,650/month with a 7-day noncurrent expiration.
findings.action: Enable versioning + Object Lock (Governance, 14 days to match rotation) with a 7-day NoncurrentVersionExpiration (~$5,650/month)

findings.title: Velero backup target is empty and unlocked
findings.description: Either EKS backups aren't running, or they go elsewhere. Object Lock is easiest to enable on a new, empty bucket, so this is the moment to do it.
findings.action: Confirm Velero is configured; recreate the bucket with Object Lock enabled while it's empty

cost_optimization.title: Evaluate S3 Intelligent-Tiering for 30 PiB of research data in S3 Standard
resources: anycompany-research-datasets-prod (30 PiB, Standard, no lifecycle transition)
cost_optimization.savings: estimate up to ~$465,000/month (~$5.6M/year); worst case +$15,000/month; ~$60,000 one-time
cost_optimization.description: Access pattern not observable from outside the account: to confirm. Intelligent-Tiering has no retrieval fees and keeps millisecond access, so the downside is limited to the monitoring fee.
cost_optimization.basis: Bucket size and storage class (CloudWatch storage metrics), 6B objects, no lifecycle transition. Saving assumes ~70% of bytes unread for 90+ days, a typical research-archive profile, not a measurement

cost_optimization.title: Close the human-error gap on 4 production datasets (83 PiB)
cost_optimization.savings: Risk reduction on 83 PiB for estimate ~$1,600/month total (measured/bounded write patterns)
cost_optimization.description: Write-once and static data creates no noncurrent versions, so versioning is almost free.
cost_optimization.basis: Measured and bounded write patterns: write-once and static data creates almost no noncurrent versions

cost_optimization.title: Stop unbounded noncurrent-version growth
cost_optimization.savings: estimate ~$14,100/month added each month avoided (~$169,000/month after a year)
cost_optimization.basis: ~600 TiB of new noncurrent versions per month that never expire; the avoided cost grows by ~$14,100/month each month (~$169,000/month after a year)

cost_optimization.title: Enable S3 Bucket Keys on high-PUT KMS buckets
cost_optimization.savings: estimate ~$5,300/month on writes alone (up to 99% fewer KMS requests)
cost_optimization.description: One-setting change; applies to new objects.
cost_optimization.basis: ~1.77B PUT requests/month × $0.03 per 10,000 KMS requests; reads add more if they also call KMS

governance._comment: Fictitious governance signals. In a real run these come from Organizations (SCPs, backup and tag policies), AWS Config, Security Hub, AWS Backup and resource tags; anything not collectable is shown as unconfirmed.
